newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: New Ireland 1996 new annual premiums up 18 pct.
newsitem.headline: New Ireland 1996 new annual premiums up 18 pct.

text.p: New Ireland Holdings Plc said on Tuesday that new annual premium sales grew to 21.8 million Irish pounds in 1996, an increase of 18 percent on the 1995 outturn.
New Ireland said 11.1 million punts of the total new premiums came from its pensions business, showing a rise of 26 percent over the previous year.
It said life annual premiums were up 11 percent at 10.7 million while single premium income amounted to 120.4 million punts, representing an increase of 31 percent on 1995.

New Ireland managing director Jack Casey said he was particularly pleased with the growth in New Ireland's pensions business. He also expressed satisfaction with growth in the life business which he said was largely due to the success of critical illness sales.

"The fact that our growth has been in the core areas of protection and pensions is very gratifying," Casey said in a results statement, adding that he was optimistic about New Ireland's performance in 1997.
"I see a number of positive factors to indicate that New Ireland can build on last year's success during 1997," Casey said.
He said with six percent economic growth forecast for the Irish economy and an increasing trend in employment figures "... the outlook remains good for the pensions market".
Casey said New Ireland will continue to target other key areas.
"We will be making some further product innovations in the critical illness area early this year and this should ensure that we maintain our strong position in this market," he said.
New Ireland is a unit of UAP Group (Union des Assurances de Paris).
